indicators.name: METR task-completion time horizon
indicators.value: ~16+ hours (50%-success horizon, Claude Mythos Preview, measured May 2026, 95% CI 8.5-55 hrs); doubling time ~105 days on the latest fit vs ~7 months long-run. METR flags measurements above 16hrs as at the edge of what its current task suite can reliably resolve (only 5 of 228 suite tasks run that long).
indicators.trend: Accelerating — doubling compressed from ~7 months to ~3.5 months in the most recent window, though the newest data point itself carries a wide confidence interval.
indicators.relevance: Core empirical proxy for autonomous-agent capability growth; feeds takeoff-speed and capability-to-power.

indicators.name: Metaculus AGI timelines
indicators.value: General AI system: community median ~Jan 2033 (25% by 2029); weakly general AI publicly known: median ~June 2028
indicators.trend: Drifted slightly later through late 2025, with renewed compression among forecasters updating in early 2026.
indicators.relevance: Aggregated forecaster judgment on how much time exists for safety work.

indicators.name: Metaculus conditional AI-catastrophe forecasts
indicators.value: Community: 50% probability of AI catastrophe conditional on AGI arriving 2025-2030; 29% for 2030-2040; 12% for 2040-2060
indicators.trend: Stable pattern: faster arrival is judged riskier across updates.
indicators.relevance: Quantifies forecaster-estimated tail risk conditional on timelines.

indicators.name: Expert P(doom) distribution
indicators.value: Persistent bimodal split ('controllable tool' vs 'uncontrollable agent' camps); ~40% of broad expert pools put >10% on catastrophic outcomes; estimates span ~0% (LeCun) to 90%+ (Yudkowsky/Yampolskiy). A narrower Feb 2026 survey of 59 x-risk/AI-safety practitioners (a self-selected, higher-concern sample) found a modal estimate of 20-29% with a secondary cluster at 50%+.
indicators.trend: No convergence in the broad expert pool; the AI-safety-insider subsample skews meaningfully higher, as expected from selection effects.
indicators.relevance: Tracks whether expert opinion converges or stays polarized — polarization itself is the headline fact.
indicators.source: 'Why do Experts Disagree on Existential Risk and P(doom)?' — https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14870 ; Summit on Existential Security survey — https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/LxuKuQd69Qx5FKhNZ/survey-of-ai-safety-leaders-on-x-risk-agi-timelines-and

indicators.name: Frontier training compute growth
indicators.value: ~4-5x per year since 2020; largest known run ~5e26 FLOP (Grok 4); models above 1e26 FLOP projected to grow from ~10 (2026) to ~80 (2028)
indicators.trend: Still exponential, increasingly gated by power and chip supply rather than capital.
indicators.relevance: Primary driver in fast-takeoff scenarios and the lever compute governance would pull.

indicators.name: Algorithmic efficiency gains
indicators.value: Compute needed for fixed performance halves roughly every 8 months (90% CI 5-14); overall ~2-6x/year efficiency improvement
indicators.trend: Steady software gains compounding on top of hardware scaling.
indicators.relevance: If compute growth slows, this is the term that decides whether capability growth slows with it — feeds rsi-binding.

indicators.name: Frontier benchmark saturation
indicators.value: ARC-AGI-2 top scores ~77-85% (not fully saturated as previously reported), which prompted ARC-AGI-3 (launched March 2026) where frontier models score under 1%; HLE top scores ~53-65% depending on tracker; FrontierMath ~52% (flat); SWE-bench Verified surged to ~95% (up from ~80%)
indicators.trend: Benchmarks are saturating faster than successors can be designed — ARC-AGI-3 launched within months of ARC-AGI-2 and immediately reset frontier scores near zero; SWE-bench Verified moved from headroom to near-saturation within the same window.
indicators.relevance: Saturation speed signals how fast capabilities outpace evaluation infrastructure.
indicators.source: ARC Prize 2025 Results — https://arcprize.org/blog/arc-prize-2025-results-analysis ; Artificial Analysis HLE — https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/humanitys-last-exam ; SWE-bench via llm-stats — https://llm-stats.com/benchmarks/swe-bench-verified

indicators.name: AI Incident Database yearly count
indicators.value: 362 incidents in 2025, up from 233 in 2024 (~55% YoY); generative AI ~58% of entries, deepfakes fastest-growing category
indicators.trend: Incident counts growing faster than aggregate deployment.
indicators.relevance: Realized, documented harms — the empirical counterpoint to purely speculative risk debates.

indicators.name: AI safety field size and funding
indicators.value: ~1,100 FTEs total (~600 technical) across ~70 organizations (2025 estimate)
indicators.trend: Growing steadily, still small relative to capabilities R&D spending.
indicators.relevance: Whether the defense side scales anywhere near capabilities investment — feeds alignment-tractability.

indicators.name: Datacenter power constraint
indicators.value: ~12 GW new US capacity announced for 2026 but only ~5 GW under construction; transformer backlog ~5 years; global datacenter demand headed toward ~84 GW by 2027
indicators.trend: Grid infrastructure now the binding constraint on frontier scaling, ahead of chips and capital.
indicators.relevance: Tests the 'compute scaling continues unabated' assumption — feeds rsi-binding and takeoff-speed.
